lines: Two small stages in 4HP: one adds a fixed voltage to its input, the other scales its input with a fader
The voltage the offset knob is added to; with nothing patched it reads 5V
Carries its input plus the offset knob, and the fader result is added to it while the fader output is unpatched
The voltage the fader scales; with nothing patched it reads 5V
Carries its input scaled by the fader, silent at the bottom and the whole input at the top
Adds between -5V and 5V to the voltage at the offset input, despite the maker's tooltip calling it an attenuverter
Scales the voltage at the fader input, from silence at the bottom to the whole of it at the top
NavControl.notes: The maker's tooltip calls param 0 an attenuverter, but the code adds its value to the input rather than scaling it; the panel prints no name for it.

lines: A bench of small utilities: two attenuating mults, an LFO, four levelled channels, two crossfaders and two signal swappers
The signal the upper mult copies, scaled by the MULT slider on its way out
Carries the upper mult input scaled by the MULT slider
Carries the upper mult input scaled by the MULT slider and inverted
Scales what the upper mult sends to its outputs, from silence to the whole input
A rising edge above 2V restarts the LFO from the start of its cycle
The LFO wave, between -5V and 5V when bipolar and 0-10V when unipolar, scaled by the LFO slider
Chooses the LFO wave: triangle in the first position and square in the other two
Sets the LFO to run bipolar between -5V and 5V, or unipolar between 0-10V
Sets the LFO frequency, doubling every volt of its setting, from 0.004Hz to 1024Hz
Scales the LFO output, from silence to the whole wave
The signal the A1 channel scales
Carries the A1 input scaled by the A1 slider, or with nothing patched whatever the A selector feeds it
Scales what reaches the A1 output
The signal the A2 channel scales
Carries the A2 input scaled by the A2 slider, or with nothing patched whatever the A selector feeds it
Scales what reaches the A2 output
The signal the B1 channel scales
Carries the B1 input scaled by the B1 slider, or with nothing patched whatever the B selector feeds it
Scales what reaches the B1 output
The signal the B2 channel scales
Carries the B2 input scaled by the B2 slider, or with nothing patched whatever the B selector feeds it
Scales what reaches the B2 output
Chooses what feeds A1 and A2 when their own jacks are empty: the VOLTAGE knob, nothing, or an inverted triangle from the LFO
Chooses what feeds B1 and B2 when their own jacks are empty: the VOLTAGE knob, nothing, or an inverted square from the LFO
Sets a fixed voltage between 0-5V for any channel whose selector is in the voltage position
Crossfades between the two A channels and the two B channels, all A at the top and all B at the bottom
Scales the crossfader output, from silence to the whole signal
The crossfade between the A channels and the B channels, scaled by the LVL knob
One of the two signals the upper swapper exchanges; with nothing patched it takes the upper mult input scaled by the MULT slider
One of the two signals the upper swapper exchanges; with nothing patched it takes the upper mult input scaled by the MULT slider and inverted
Carries the B swap input while the swap button is unlit and the A swap input while it is lit
Carries the A swap input while the swap button is unlit and the B swap input while it is lit
Exchanges the two upper swap outputs, one press over and the next back
The signal the lower mult copies, scaled by the lower MULT knob on its way out
Carries the lower mult input scaled by the lower MULT knob
Carries the lower mult input scaled by the lower MULT knob and inverted
Scales what the lower mult sends to its outputs, from silence to the whole input
One of the two signals the lower swapper exchanges
Carries the lower B swap input while the lower swap button is unlit and the lower A swap input while it is lit
Carries the lower A swap input while the lower swap button is unlit and the lower B swap input while it is lit
Exchanges the two lower swap outputs, one press over and the next back
One of the two signals the lower crossfader mixes between
The crossfade between the two lower fade inputs
Crossfades between the two lower fade inputs, all A fully clockwise and all B fully anticlockwise
Nothing in the module reads this jack; what feeds the A and B channels when their own inputs are empty is set by the A and B selectors
Bench.notes: IN A and IN B (inputs 9 and 10) are declared and placed on the panel but never read in this build, so they have no line and no tag. Input 15 is declared with no widget. The mult, swap, channel and crossfade jacks carry whatever is patched into them, so they are left without a family.

lines: Four function generators, each slewing towards its input voltage at its own rise and fall times, with a curve control, a manual trigger and a looping switch
Sets the time range of that channel: medium from 0.01 to 10 seconds, fast from 1ms to 1 second, or slow from 0.1 to 102 seconds
Bends both slopes of that channel, logarithmic anticlockwise, straight at noon and exponential clockwise
Sets how long that channel takes to rise, from the shortest time of its range at the bottom to a thousand times that at the top
Sets how long that channel takes to fall, from the shortest time of its range at the bottom to a thousand times that at the top
Starts that channel's envelope by hand, taking it to 10V and then letting it fall
A rising edge above 2V starts that channel's envelope, taking it to 10V and then letting it fall
Switches looping on and off for that channel, one press on and the next off
A rising edge switches looping on or off for that channel
Adds to the rise time of that channel, 10V covering the whole of the range
Adds to the fall time of that channel, 10V covering the whole of the range
The voltage that channel slews towards
The slewed output of that channel
Five transposers for pitch voltages, two working in octaves, two in semitones and one in fractions of a semitone
Shifts the pitch in whole octaves, four down to four up
The pitch voltage the octave section transposes
Every 2V here shifts the pitch a whole octave, rounded to the nearest octave and added to the knob; this jack drives both octave sections
The pitch from the octave input, shifted by the knob and by the octave CV
Shifts the pitch in whole semitones, six down to six up
The pitch voltage the semitone section transposes
Every 2V here shifts the pitch a whole semitone, rounded to the nearest semitone and added to the knob
The pitch from the semitone input, shifted by the knob and by the semitone CV
Shifts the pitch by a fraction of a semitone, a semitone down to a semitone up, without stepping
The pitch voltage the fine section transposes
A quarter of the voltage here is added to the pitch, so 4V shifts it a whole octave
The pitch from the fine input, shifted by the knob and by the fine CV
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the octave CV jack of the first octave section shifts both of them
Transpose.notes: Input 5, the CV jack of the second octave section, is not read in this build: the code applies input 4 to both octave sections, so input 5 is left without a line or a tag. Fixed in the maker's later source.

lines: Three pitch shifters into one quantiser: each shifts its input by octaves, semitones and a fine amount, and the result is snapped to a root note and scale shown on the display
Shifts that column in whole octaves, four down to four up
Shifts that column in whole semitones, five down to five up
Shifts that column by a fraction of a semitone, a semitone down to a semitone up; it is added after quantising, so it is not snapped to the scale
The pitch voltage that column shifts and quantises
Every 2V here shifts that column a whole octave, rounded to the nearest octave
Every 2V here shifts that column a whole semitone, rounded to the nearest semitone
A quarter of the voltage here is added to that column after quantising
That column's shifted and quantised pitch
Sends the first column's input to the second column, in place of anything patched there
Sends the second column's input to the third column, in place of anything patched there
Sets the root note the scale is built on, the twelve semitones from C to B
Chooses the scale all three columns are quantised to: seventeen scales and a last position that leaves the pitch unquantised
0-10V sweeps the root note through the twelve semitones, added to the root knob
0-10V sweeps the scale through the list, added to the scale knob
Utility.notes: Params 13 to 15 are declared but have no widget on the panel and are never read.

lines: Builds a four note chord from one pitch, with root, third, fifth and seventh on their own outputs and four voices arranged by an inversion and a voicing control
The pitch the chord is built from; the octave is discarded and only the note within it is used
Transposes the whole chord in semitones, six down at the far left and six up at the far right
Transposes the whole chord in semitones, scaled by the offset attenuator, 1.5V to a semitone at full
Attenuates the offset CV, from nothing to its whole range
Steps the four voices through four inversions, changing which note of the chord becomes the lowest voice
Steps through the inversions, scaled by the inversion attenuator, 3V to a step at full
Attenuates the inversion CV, from nothing to its whole range
Steps through five voicings, each dropping or raising the second and fourth voice by an octave
Steps through the voicings, scaled by the voicing attenuator, 3V to a step at full
Attenuates the voicing CV, from nothing to its whole range
The root of the chord, within one octave of 0V
The third of the chord, four semitones above the root until an alteration moves it
The fifth of the chord, seven semitones above the root until an alteration moves it
The seventh of the chord, eleven semitones above the root until an alteration moves it
The first voice of the chord, as the inversion and voicing arrange it
The second voice of the chord, as the inversion and voicing arrange it
The third voice of the chord, as the inversion and voicing arrange it
The fourth voice of the chord, as the inversion and voicing arrange it
Lowers the third to three semitones above the root
A rising edge lowers the third to three semitones above the root
Lowers the fifth to six semitones above the root
A rising edge lowers the fifth to six semitones above the root
Lowers the seventh to ten semitones above the root
A rising edge lowers the seventh to ten semitones above the root
Lowers the seventh to nine semitones above the root
A rising edge lowers the seventh to nine semitones above the root
Raises the fifth to eight semitones above the root
A rising edge raises the fifth to eight semitones above the root
Replaces the root voice with the note two semitones above the root
A rising edge replaces the root voice with the note two semitones above the root
Raises the third to five semitones above the root
A rising edge raises the third to five semitones above the root
Raises the fifth to nine semitones above the root
A rising edge raises the fifth to nine semitones above the root
Raises the seventh to the octave above the root
A rising edge raises the seventh to the octave above the root
Replaces the root voice with the note one semitone above the root
A rising edge replaces the root voice with the note one semitone above the root
Replaces the root voice with the note three semitones above the root
A rising edge replaces the root voice with the note three semitones above the root
Note — in this build an alteration holds for only the instant its button is pressed or its jack is triggered; the lamp stays lit but the notes go back to the plain chord
Chord.notes: In the installed 2.1 build the eleven alteration buttons set their note only on the sample the trigger fires, because the assignment sits inside the Schmitt trigger's if block; the lamp toggles and holds. The maker's later source moves the assignment out of the if block so the alteration holds. The lines describe the alteration each control makes, with a Note line about the one-sample behaviour.

lines: A 4-by-4 grid sequencer: two clocks walk a cursor over the grid, and the knob it lands on is quantised to the root note and scale on the display
A rising edge steps the cursor one cell across, and at the end of the row it wraps and moves to the next row unless the X lock is on
A rising edge steps the cursor one cell down, and at the bottom of the column it wraps and moves to the next column unless the Y lock is on
A rising edge puts the cursor back in the first column
A rising edge puts the cursor back in the top row
Reverses both clocks, so the X clock steps across to the left and the Y clock steps up
A rising edge reverses both clocks, so the X clock steps across to the left and the Y clock steps up
Keeps the cursor on its own row when the X clock wraps round the end
A rising edge switches the X lock on or off
Keeps the cursor in its own column when the Y clock wraps round the end
A rising edge switches the Y lock on or off
Sets the pitch of that cell, -2V to 2V before quantising
Switches that cell's gate on or off, one press on and the next off
Sets the root note the scale is built on, the twelve semitones from C to B
0-10V sweeps the root note through the twelve semitones, added to the KEY knob
Chooses the scale the grid is quantised to: seventeen scales and a last position that leaves the knob voltages unquantised
0-10V sweeps the scale through the list, added to the SCALE knob
The quantised pitch of the cell the cursor is on, held at its last value until the cursor reaches another cell whose gate is on
Carries 10V while the cursor is on a cell whose gate is on
A 1ms trigger as the cursor leaves a cell whose gate is on
The quantised pitch of the knob in that column, on whichever row the cursor is on
The quantised pitch of the knob in that row, on whichever column the cursor is on
Pressing this switches its lamp, but nothing in the module reads it: both clocks take their direction from the X direction button
A rising edge switches the Y direction lamp, but nothing in the module reads it: both clocks take their direction from the X direction button
Note — a BenePads placed immediately to the right moves the cursor to the pad being held and opens the gate output while it is held
Bene.notes: The Y direction button (param 5) and its jack (input 6) only toggle a lamp in this build: both clocks read the X direction flag, so neither gets a line or a tag. Inputs 10 to 13 have no widget on the panel.

lines: Sixteen pads that pick a cell on a Bene, and goes immediately to the right of it
Holding this pad moves the Bene's cursor to the matching cell of its grid and holds the Bene's gate output high
BenePads.notes: The three outputs are declared in the code but their widgets are commented out, so they have no place on the panel and no line.

lines: A six channel scanning mixer: a window is slid across the inputs and what falls under it is mixed to three outputs
The signal of that channel, scaled by that channel's level trimmer before the scan reaches it
